title: Ainsworth Opens With a Statement
body:
Ainsworth's 165.56 was the week's high score, but the real story is how he got there: Kenneth Walker III (32.6) and D'Andre Swift (31.9) combined for 64.5 points at running back - with David Montgomery (27.4) still sitting on the bench behind them. The resulting 97.06-point demolition of Zogg is the biggest Week 1-2 margin specifically in 13 years of NWL history, shattering the old Week 1-2 mark (Muenchow's 67.98-point win over Stover, 2022) by 29 points - though it's not the biggest blowout in league history overall; that's still Conlin's 127.6-point win over Zogg in Week 3, 2019. It is a career-best opening two weeks for Ainsworth personally, who'd never topped 237.9 combined through Week 2 before (2020). Zogg's day was rough top to bottom: nobody on the roster cracked 17 points, including first-round pick CeeDee Lamb (12.9), and the Chargers' Head Coach bonus actively cost him 5 points.

The league's best individual performance belonged to Caleb Williams (37.3) - an 8th-round pick who outscored every quarterback drafted ahead of him and powered Muenchow past Pfaffinger, 133.46-95.3. Glaser's 152.9 (2nd-best team score of the week) rode Derrick Henry (34.8) and Christian Watson (29.7) past Palaia, while 11th-round pick Jalen Coker quietly dropped 29.8 from the bench - a lineup call that didn't end up mattering in a 48-point win. Conlin needed just 129.86 to handle Hagan (78.02), with Josh Allen's 35.7 the league's second-best individual number of the week.

The nightcap was the only real nail-biter: Larson held off Prodahl 101.86-87.92, a 13.94-point margin. Goetz beat Stover 108.06-85.46 behind Jahmyr Gibbs (31.1), the draft's own first overall pick, to round out the slate.

Six games, five double-digit margins, and a Week 1-2 scoring record on the books - Week 1 wasted no time separating the contenders from the rest.

title: Zogg Bounces Back, Three Teams Start 2-0
body:
A week after absorbing the biggest Week 1-2 beating in 13 years of NWL history, Zogg answered with the week's high score - 138.86 - led by CeeDee Lamb (31.3, more than double his Week 1 output) and 11th-round pick Dak Prescott (29.8), to knock off Goetz (75.6) and get back in the win column. The response looks dramatic, but the numbers say otherwise: Zogg's 207.4 combined two-week total is almost exactly his 13-year career average (207.1) for this point in a season - Week 1 was the outlier, not Week 2.

Ainsworth, Glaser, and Larson all won again to open the season 2-0, the only unbeaten teams left in the league - though it means very different things for each of them. Ainsworth's 283.8 and Glaser's 265.9 are both career bests through two weeks, blowing past their previous personal highs (237.9 and 207.4, both set in 2020) by 86-94 points. Larson's 203.5, by contrast, is almost dead-even with his own career average - proof that this league's power rankings (which weigh scoring and all-play expected wins, not just the win-loss record) have him 3rd rather than 1st for a reason.

Hagan bounced back from a rough Week 1 to beat Pfaffinger 105.06-70.9, even after starting Jalen Hurts (16.2) over a Brock Purdy (28.5, a 13th-round pick) sitting on the bench - a decision that would have flipped a closer game. Pfaffinger's own Bryce Young, picked up as a free agent the same week, delivered 24.1 points in his Pfaffinger debut. Larson handled Palaia 101.68-58.84 - the week's lowest score - behind Patrick Mahomes' 29.0.

The closest game of the week came at the bottom of the standings: Prodahl edged Stover 84.92-72.98, an 11.94-point margin. Through two weeks, Pfaffinger, Palaia, and Stover are all 0-2, and the gap between the top and bottom of the league is already starting to show.

title: Glaser Stays Perfect, Benches Decide Week 3
body:
Glaser is 3-0 again. Jaxon Smith-Njigba (30.4) and Derrick Henry (21.4) carried a 113.14-106.34 win over Larson, even with Kenyon Sadiq (20.0) and Juwan Johnson (19.3) on the bench while Dalton Schultz started and scored 4.5. Glaser also opened 2025 at 3-0, which makes him the first manager in NWL history to start back-to-back seasons 3-0 - none of the 17 teams that started 3-0 from 2013-2025 had ever done it twice in a row. History is encouraging: 16 of those 17 made the playoffs. The one that didn't was Conlin in 2018, who started 3-0 and still finished 7th. Last year's 3-0 Glaser only finished 6th, so nobody should print the banner yet.

The loudest part of Week 3 was the benches. Larson lost that game by 6.80 with Michael Wilson (20.4) and Terry McLaurin (16.7) on the bench while Devaughn Vele (5.4) started. The Wilson-for-Vele swap alone was worth 15 points. Ainsworth, the league's leading scorer at 382.9 points, lost 101.28-99.10 to Stover in the closest game of the season. Ainsworth's Ravens Head Coach scored +5 on the bench, so starting the coach wins it by 2.82. Stover's first win of the year came partly from Kalif Raymond (18.0) in the flex, a sentence nobody had on their bingo card.

Hagan did it the other way around. Brock Purdy scored 31.3, the most by any quarterback in the league this week, from Hagan's bench, while Jalen Hurts started and scored 12.6. Hagan won anyway, 85.62-68.84, because the opponent was Zogg. Zogg has now scored under 70 twice in three weeks (68.50 in Week 1, 68.84 here), with the Week 2 high score of 138.86 in between. The Bengals Head Coach cost him 5 points. That's 7 sub-70 regular-season games for Zogg since the current scoring era started in 2022. Hagan is 2-1 despite a negative point differential (268.7 for, 269.6 against).

Palaia put up the week's high score, 132.16, behind Bijan Robinson (34.3) and Brock Bowers (22.6), and beat Pfaffinger by 59.02. Pfaffinger opened 2025 at 3-0 and is now 0-3. It's his third 0-3 start (2020, 2022, 2026), tied with Hagan, Goetz, and Larson for the most in league history. Pfaffinger's 370.7 points against lead the league by 42.5 and rank 9th-most through three weeks in NWL history. None of the 18 teams that started 0-3 from 2013-2025 won a title, and only 4 made the playoffs. Still, Pfaffinger has escaped this before: the 2020 team faced 394.8 points in its first three games (2nd-most ever), started 0-3, and finished 5th.

Elsewhere: Jahmyr Gibbs scored 37.9, the most of any player this week, and Goetz beat Prodahl 121.34-103.86. Prodahl started Drake Maye (3.8) with Kyler Murray (10.4) on the bench. Muenchow handled Conlin 102.50-81.06 behind Garrett Wilson (21.7) and Matthew Stafford (20.9). Conlin left Jordan Addison (17.5) on the bench and has now lost two straight.

Week 4's headliner is #1 vs. #2: Glaser hosts Ainsworth with ESPN favoring Glaser by 11. The all-time series is tied 12-12, and their last meeting (Week 10, 2025) went to Ainsworth 113.54-112.20. The week's biggest spread belongs to Prodahl, favored by 18 over Zogg.

title: Pfaffinger Wins One, Glaser Wins With Two Zeros
body:
Pfaffinger is off the schneid. He beat Conlin 110-89 for his first win of the season, with Bhayshul Tuten (23), Bryce Young (20), and DeMario Douglas (16) doing the work. That keeps him out of the 0-6 club. Only two teams have started 0-6, and neither stopped there: Larson (2015) went to 0-7, and Goetz (2025) to 0-8, the worst start in NWL history. The bad news: 17 teams have been 1-5 after six games, and none of them made the playoffs.

Week 6 was ugly for everybody. The league averaged 89.9 points, 9.5% below the 2026 average of 99.3, and only three teams reached 100. Prodahl's 115 was the top score. Measured against its own season's average (the fair way to compare across scoring eras), that's the 13th-worst week of 185 since 2013. The worst is still Week 1 of 2023, when the league averaged 79.1, 18.6% below that season, and nobody reached 100. Week 6 of 2022 was 13.1% below its season, and only one team reached 100 that week. By raw average this week was only 47th-lowest, because scoring before 2018 was so much lower: the 2013 season averaged 84.1.

{{visual:low-weeks}}

{{visual:week6-scores}}

Glaser won with two starters at zero. Cam Skattebo and Juwan Johnson both played and scored 0 (Johnson was targeted twice and caught nothing), and the Colts Head Coach added -5. Glaser still beat Zogg 81-61 because Trevor Lawrence scored 27. From 2022-2025, a team started two zero-point players (not counting Head Coaches) 11 times in the regular season and won three of them. Glaser is the fourth. He also had Stefon Diggs (13), Blake Corum (13), and Keenan Allen (12) on the bench, and has left 140 points on the bench this season, the most in the league. Zogg's 61.1 is the second-lowest score of 2026, just above Palaia's 58.8 in Week 2.

Stover beat Larson 81-73 for his fourth straight win, the longest active streak in the league. His 81.0 is the lowest winning score of 2026, just under Glaser's 81.1 from the same week. Stover is 4-2 but has the fewest expected wins of any team with a winning record (2.2), and he's played the hardest schedule so far. He has been very good at being lucky.

Ainsworth beat Muenchow 107-98 and is back to #1 in the power rankings. Kenneth Walker III scored 27 and D'Andre Swift 21, and Ainsworth won despite Tyler Shough scoring 27 on his bench (Jordan Love started and scored 20). Ainsworth and Glaser are both 5-1. From 2013-2025, 14 teams started 5-1, 13 made the playoffs, and 4 won the title.

Elsewhere: Prodahl beat Hagan 115-84 behind Drake Maye (24) and Germie Bernard (20). It's Prodahl's second straight win, and his playoff odds jumped 16 points to 65%, the biggest gain of the week. Hagan has lost three straight and started Darren Waller, who was targeted twice and scored 0, with Ryan Flournoy (14) on the bench. Goetz beat Palaia 91.9-87.4, the closest game of the week, behind Malik Nabers (23). That evened their all-time series at 12-12, and at 24 games it's now the most-played tied rivalry in league history. Pfaffinger's win did the same to his series with Conlin, now 11-11. Larson's playoff odds fell 14 points to 34%, the biggest drop.

Only five of the twelve Head Coaches in lineups won this week. Conlin and Palaia both started a coach whose team was on bye, the Lions and the Vikings, for 0 points each. Detroit and Minnesota were two of the four teams with Week 6 byes.

Best-ball standings didn't change this week. Through six weeks, four teams have a different best-ball record: Prodahl would be 4-2 and Pfaffinger 2-4, while Goetz would be 3-3 and Zogg 1-5.

{{visual:best-ball}}

In Week 7, #1 Ainsworth plays #5 Prodahl in the game of the week. It's projected as the highest-scoring game (224), and Prodahl is favored by 1. Prodahl also leads the all-time series 14-2. Conlin has Buffalo on bye, which takes out Josh Allen and James Cook III, so Larson is favored by 26.5, the biggest spread of the week. Hagan and Goetz is a pick'em (Goetz by 0.5), and Goetz leads that series 13-3. Buffalo, Jacksonville, the Chargers, and Washington are on bye.
